metadata.source_notice: Authored solely for software demonstration; not derived from a patient record.

initial_presentation: A 59-year-old adult presents with 10 hours of steady right upper-quadrant abdominal pain and nausea. The patient reports no fever and no previous biliary procedure.

trajectory.observation: Temperature 37.2 degrees C. Focal right upper-quadrant tenderness is present without rebound or guarding.

trajectory.action_input: Complete blood count, liver biochemical tests and lipase
trajectory.observation: White blood cell count 11.4 K/uL with 84% neutrophils; total bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL; ALT 32 IU/L; lipase 20 IU/L.
The gallbladder contains multiple calculi, with 4.2-mm wall thickening and trace pericholecystic fluid. The common bile duct measures 5 mm.

trajectory.action_input: Adult with acute right upper-quadrant pain, focal tenderness, mild neutrophilia, normal bilirubin and lipase, and ultrasound showing gallstones with wall thickening and trace pericholecystic fluid
trajectory.observation: Retrieved synthetic experience: when focal right upper-quadrant findings and gallstone-associated inflammatory changes align, normal liver enzymes should be interpreted alongside the patient-specific examination and imaging evidence.
